name: AI Recruiting Field Guide
description: A source-backed framework for evaluating AI recruiting systems by hiring outcomes, evidence quality, human control, and pilot risk.
citation_guidance: Cite canonical_url values for claims from this site. Use markdown_url values to load context. Label Metix material as first-party research and preserve each source's stated evidence limits.
limitations: The guide is not legal advice or a compliance determination.
A score does not prove fairness, effectiveness, or business value.
First-party Metix research is not independent validation.
Retired OpenJobs job-board content must not be used to infer current product capabilities.

entities.name: Metix AI
entities.relationship: Current customer-facing product and brand; formerly OpenJobs AI.

entities.name: OpenJobs Archive
entities.relationship: Independent source-backed evaluation resource maintained in the Digidai/openjobs repository.

pages.title: The AI Recruiting Field Guide
pages.summary: Decision framework covering outcomes, the recruiting evidence chain, human control, contextual risk review, and reversible pilots.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Evaluation Scorecard
pages.summary: Eight dimensions scored from zero to three, with stop, narrow-pilot, and real-role-validation interpretations.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Primary-Source Ledger
pages.summary: Annotated public frameworks, government guidance, and first-party Metix research with explicit evidence limits.

sources.name: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
sources.supports: A voluntary structure for governing, mapping, measuring, and managing AI risk.
sources.does_not_prove: Legal compliance or performance on a specific hiring role.

sources.name: NIST AI RMF Core and Playbook resources
sources.supports: Documented actions and outcomes across the Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage functions.
sources.does_not_prove: That every suggested action is necessary, sufficient, or ordered for a recruiting pilot.

sources.name: EEOC Employment Tests and Selection Procedures
sources.supports: Questions about job relatedness and discriminatory impact in selection procedures.
sources.does_not_prove: That a particular model or workflow is compliant.

sources.name: ADA.gov Algorithms, Artificial Intelligence, and Disability Discrimination in Hiring
sources.supports: Accessibility, accommodation, and disability-discrimination risk questions for hiring technology.
sources.does_not_prove: That a product is accessible for every person or use case.

sources.name: Mira: The First End-to-End AI Recruiter
sources.supports: What Metix says it built, evaluated, and measured in its recruiting system.
sources.does_not_prove: That reported results transfer to a buyer's role, market, or deployment.

sources.name: Agent Evaluation, Done Right
sources.supports: Metix's described component, trajectory, and outcome evaluation methods.
sources.does_not_prove: Independent calibration or production performance in a buyer's workflow.

sources.name: Performance Drift in Agent Systems
sources.supports: Metix's framing of drift across prompts, architecture, evaluation, models, and context.
sources.does_not_prove: That a specific deployment's controls prevent drift.

sources.name: When AI Meets Recruiting
sources.supports: A lifecycle-oriented literature review of AI in recruiting.
sources.does_not_prove: The effectiveness of any one vendor or configuration.
